clue.text: Virtue is a solitary pastime

definitions.meaning: the quality of waiting calmly without complaint, one of the classic virtues
the card game played alone, called solitaire in America

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the forbearing virtue and the one-player card game, so each half is a straight sense.

clue.text: Tract presenting the Apostle's core convictions

indicators.note: the core of a word is its central letter, here taken from the seven letters of Apostle

parts.note: a creed is a set of firmly held beliefs

explanation.surface: A pamphlet setting out the essential beliefs of St Paul or the Apostles' Creed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to the Apostles' Creed, but only the middle letter S of APOSTLE is used, with CREED after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A long written discourse or pamphlet, a tract, is also called by this word for a lengthy harangue.

clue.text: Evil One rising in disorder, a restless spirit

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, the disorder word enclosing the rest

parts.note: gout is a disorder of the joints

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: evil means bad
one is the indefinite article a

explanation.surface: The Devil ascending amid chaos, an unquiet soul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evil One' reads as a name for Satan, but the two words work separately; 'rising' turns them to ADAB in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who wanders restlessly from place to place in search of pleasure is a gadabout.

clue.text: Quantity of Richard III's desire?

definitions.meaning: a total or sum of something
in Shakespeare Richard III cries for a horse, that is, for something to ride

explanation.surface: Asking how much Shakespeare's Richard III wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's king cries 'A horse! A horse! My kingdom for a horse!', so what he wants is A MOUNT; the question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An amount is a quantity, the sum or total of something.

clue.text: Celebrity going to Switzerland for a stiffener

parts.note: a celebrity is a star
CH is the international code for Switzerland (Confoederatio Helvetica)

explanation.surface: A famous person heads to Switzerland to get a stiff drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch is used to stiffen fabric such as shirt collars, so it is a stiffener.

clue.text: Cry from the heart of Basques, unanimously

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central part, here the three middle letters of Basques

parts.note: done unanimously means done by all

explanation.surface: A shout from deep within the Basque people, all of one voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A squall is a loud harsh cry, as of a baby, as well as a sudden storm.

clue.text: Priests holding mass at religious festival

indicators.note: one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: lamas are Tibetan Buddhist priests
m is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: Clergy celebrating Mass at a church feast.
explanation.walkthrough: LAMMAS (1 August) is the old English harvest festival when loaves made from the first wheat were blessed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lammas is the traditional English harvest feast of the loaf, a religious festival.

clue.text: Back in a very short time

definitions.meaning: to back a proposal is to support it formally
a moment, as in 'just a sec'

explanation.definitionFit: To second a motion is to back it, and a sixtieth of a minute is a tiny span of time.

clue.text: Musical form of saga getting spacial realignment

indicators.note: realignment means the letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A piece of music based on an epic tale, with its space rearranged.
explanation.walkthrough: SAGA and SPACIAL together are rearranged, signalled by 'realignment'.
explanation.definitionFit: A passacaglia is a slow Baroque musical form built on a repeated bass line.

clue.text: Girl without leg stretched out

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the girl's name goes around the other piece

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name
a pin is slang for a leg

explanation.surface: A young woman missing a limb lies flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it has its old sense of 'outside', so the girl's name wraps around the leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Supine means lying flat on the back, stretched out face upwards.

clue.text: Mixed-up Coca Cola Company removed from Mexican resort

indicators.note: mixed means the letters are jumbled together into a new order
removed means some letters are taken away from the jumbled pool

explanation.surface: A muddled soft-drink firm is ousted from a Mexican holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed-up' is split: 'Mixed' signals the anagram and 'up' joins the drink's name as fodder; 'removed' takes the company abbreviation out of that pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Acapulco is a famous Pacific beach resort city in Mexico.

clue.text: Sorry-sounding officer slicing vegetable, perhaps

indicators.note: one piece cuts into the other, sitting inside it

parts.note: a vegetable is an example of a plant, as the 'perhaps' warns
GEN is the abbreviation for general, a senior officer

explanation.surface: An apologetic officer chopping up vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sorry' here is the old sense of sad or wretched, not apologetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Plangent describes a loud, mournful sound, so it is sorry-sounding in the sense of sad.

clue.text: Record being played in front of mobile home causes unrest

parts.note: a record is a disc
a record being played is on
a tent is a home you can carry about

explanation.surface: Music played outside a caravan stirs up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mobile home' suggests a caravan or trailer, but it means a shelter you carry. 'In front of' only sets the order of the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Discontent is dissatisfaction, which in a population shows as unrest.

clue.text: Oppression involves putting tube into each part

parts.note: per means each, as in so much per head

indicators.note: one piece is put into the other

parts.note: a section is a part
the Tube is London's Underground, abbreviated U

explanation.surface: Tyranny means sticking pipes into every section.
explanation.walkthrough: London's Underground railway is called the Tube, and U stands for Underground; it goes into SECTION after PER.
explanation.definitionFit: Persecution is cruel, sustained ill-treatment, a form of oppression.

clue.text: Horoscope includes love, thanks to noble Pole

indicators.note: the first word holds the next inside it

parts.note: a horoscope column is informally called the stars
love is nil in tennis, so the letter O
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A star-sign reading with affection, by courtesy of a Polish aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: A starosta was a Polish noble holding a royal estate or office.
explanation.definitionFit: A starosta was a Polish nobleman given charge of a district, so a noble Pole.

clue.text: Very exciting alternative to fuel before 1099

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
gas is a fuel
in Roman numerals M is 1000 and IC can stand for 99, one less than a hundred

explanation.surface: Another option for fuel before the year 1099.
explanation.walkthrough: IC for 99 is not strict Roman usage (which writes XCIX), but it is a common crossword liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: Orgasmic is used loosely to mean thrilling or intensely exciting.

clue.text: So upbeat a piece!

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to tan someone is to beat them

explanation.surface: Such a cheerful little composition!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upbeat' splits into 'up', the reversal signal in this down clue, and 'beat', which turned upwards gives NAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonata is a musical piece for one or two instruments.

clue.text: Bring on the popular dictator

parts.note: something popular is in
Il Duce was the title of Mussolini, the Italian dictator

explanation.surface: Wheel out the well-liked strongman.
explanation.definitionFit: To induce labour is to bring it on, so the two phrases are synonyms.

clue.text: Many curse the deadly sin of the garment-bearer

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100, so many
an oath is a curse or swear word
anger, or wrath, is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: Lots of swearing shows the wrath of the one carrying clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the shaped hook-topped frame on which a coat or shirt hangs, so it bears a garment.

clue.text: Almost due time to break monotony

indicators.note: to break means the letters are smashed into a new order
almost means the final letter is dropped from the phrase

explanation.surface: It is nearly time to put an end to the boredom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the last letter of DUE TIME, leaving DUETIM, and 'to break' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedium is wearisome sameness, the same thing as monotony.

clue.text: Come back with a profit

definitions.meaning: to come back is to go home again
the yield earned on an investment

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to go back to a place and the gain or yield on money invested.

clue.text: See 11
Note about an entrance to a culinary style

indicators.note: about means going around the other pieces

parts.note: ti is a note of the sol-fa scale
a door is an entrance

explanation.surface: A musical note concerning the doorway to a style of cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Tandoori is the Indian way of cooking in a clay oven, a style of cuisine.

clue.text: Model to come out displaying fabric

parts.note: the Model T was the early Ford car, so model gives T
to issue is to emerge or come out

explanation.surface: A fashion model emerges wearing cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' suggests a catwalk; it is the Ford Model T.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue is a fine, light woven fabric, such as gold tissue.

clue.text: Sharpness of turn in a built-up area

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a city is a large built-up area
a U-turn, so turn gives U

explanation.surface: Keenness of a U-turn in town.
explanation.definitionFit: Acuity means keenness or sharpness, of vision or thought.

clue.text: One getting into pot has a big trip

indicators.note: one piece gets inside the other

parts.note: a cruse is an old word for a small pot or jar
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone climbing into a pot is having a great voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruise is a long voyage, a big trip at sea.
